headline: Tk 276.30 crore embezzlement: ACC approves case against Sheikh Hasina, Rehana
summary: The case involves the alleged misappropriation of corporate social responsibility (CSR) funds intended for the Bangabandhu Memorial Trust.
details: The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) has approved a case against ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina and her sister Sheikh Rehana.
The duo, along with former Exim Bank chairman Mohammad Nazrul Islam Mazumder, are accused of embezzling Tk 276.30 crore.
The funds were collected from various banks as corporate social responsibility (CSR) funds specifically for the Bangabandhu Memorial Trust.
ACC Secretary Saidur Rahman Khan confirmed the approval of the case during a press briefing at the commission’s headquarters yesterday.
caption:
Tk 276.30 crore in CSR funds allegedly embezzled. The ACC has now approved a case against Sheikh Hasina and Sheikh Rehana.

The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) has approved a case against ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina and her sister Sheikh Rehana.

The duo, along with former Exim Bank chairman Mohammad Nazrul Islam Mazumder, are accused of embezzling Tk 276.30 crore.

The funds were collected from various banks as corporate social responsibility (CSR) funds specifically for the Bangabandhu Memorial Trust.

ACC Secretary Saidur Rahman Khan confirmed the approval of the case during a press briefing at the commission’s headquarters yesterday.

headline_marked: Govt moves to [[replace RAB with Special Response Battalion]] under new law
headline: Govt moves to replace RAB with Special Response Battalion under new law
summary: A bill has been introduced in Parliament to abolish the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) and establish the SRB as a specialized unit under the police force.
details: Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed introduced the 'Special Response Battalion (SRB) Act, 2026' bill in the National Parliament on Thursday. The bill proposes the abolition of the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) and the creation of the SRB as a specialized unit under the police force.

The Home Minister stated that the government's manifesto and public demand were to abolish RAB. However, he emphasized the need for an elite force under the police to combat modern challenges, including cybercrime, gambling, and narcotics.

The proposed SRB will be a modern, professional, and accountable unit tasked with protecting public security and suppressing terrorism and organized crime. The bill emphasizes transparency, oversight, and effective accountability in the exercise of the force's powers.

The SRB will be headquartered in Dhaka and led by a Director General, who will be an officer of at least Additional Inspector General of Police rank. It will be composed of personnel from the police and other disciplined forces.

Key responsibilities of the SRB will include combating terrorism, organized crime, illegal arms, narcotics, cybercrime, and disappearances. It will also handle cases of human trafficking, kidnapping, and crimes against women and children.

The bill was sent to the parliamentary standing committee on the Ministry of Home Affairs for further scrutiny. Opposition leaders requested more time for review, and it was agreed that the bill would be returned within four working days.
caption:
RAB is set to be abolished. A new 'Special Response Battalion' (SRB) will take its place as an elite police unit.

Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed introduced the 'Special Response Battalion (SRB) Act, 2026' bill in the National Parliament on Thursday. The bill proposes the abolition of the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) and the creation of the SRB as a specialized unit under the police force.

The Home Minister stated that the government's manifesto and public demand were to abolish RAB. However, he emphasized the need for an elite force under the police to combat modern challenges, including cybercrime, gambling, and narcotics.

The proposed SRB will be a modern, professional, and accountable unit tasked with protecting public security and suppressing terrorism and organized crime. The bill emphasizes transparency, oversight, and effective accountability in the exercise of the force's powers.

The SRB will be headquartered in Dhaka and led by a Director General, who will be an officer of at least Additional Inspector General of Police rank. It will be composed of personnel from the police and other disciplined forces.

Key responsibilities of the SRB will include combating terrorism, organized crime, illegal arms, narcotics, cybercrime, and disappearances. It will also handle cases of human trafficking, kidnapping, and crimes against women and children.

The bill was sent to the parliamentary standing committee on the Ministry of Home Affairs for further scrutiny. Opposition leaders requested more time for review, and it was agreed that the bill would be returned within four working days.
